readings.title: A Christmas Plan in Our Town
readings.article:
Christmas is near, and the people in our town are eager. They read a Bible story and use Latin words together. From a new angle, they plan a good day for everyone.

People calculate the frequency of each program and its composition. They use this to generate a rapid plan. They keep their privacy and do not tell names to others.
readings.translation:
圣诞节临近了，我们镇上的人们都很期待。他们读一个《圣经》故事，并一起使用拉丁语词汇。他们从一个新的角度，为大家筹划美好的一天。

人们计算每个节目的频率及其构成。他们用这个来生成一个快速的计划。他们保护自己的隐私，不把名字告诉别人。

questions.evidence: They read a Bible story and use Latin words together.

questions.question: What do people calculate?
options: The privacy of each person
The angle of each program
The frequency of each program
The names of each person
questions.explanation: 原文明确说人们计算每个节目的频率及其构成，所以选 The frequency of each program。
questions.evidence: People calculate the frequency of each program and its composition.

questions.question: What do people do with their privacy?
options: They share it with everyone
They keep it and hide names
They write it in a Bible
They calculate it each day
questions.explanation: 原文说他们保护隐私、不把名字告诉别人，可推知他们守住隐私、不透露名字。
questions.evidence: They keep their privacy and do not tell names to others.

segments.goal: 介绍圣诞节临近，人们用拉丁语歌曲和《圣经》故事准备庆祝。

描述节日当天大家再次唱歌，圣诞气氛再次产生。

readings.title: A Latin Christmas
readings.article:
In many Latin towns, Christmas comes on the same day each year. People calculate the day with an angle of light. They look up and write the number down. The number helps them plan the Christmas food.

At Christmas, people read the Latin bible. The high frequency of this can generate a rapid change across the room. Some people care about privacy when others can hear them.

The composition of this Christmas Bible reading is clear. It can generate rapid music across a whole room, and the Latin words stay in the mind long after the reading ends.
readings.translation:
在许多拉丁城镇，圣诞节每年都在同一天到来。人们用光的角度来计算这一天。他们抬头看，把数字写下来。这个数字帮助他们计划圣诞食物。

在圣诞节，人们读拉丁文圣经。这样做的高频率能在整个房间里产生迅速的变化。当别人能听见时，有些人会在意隐私。

这次圣诞圣经阅读的构成很清楚。它能在整个房间里产生迅速的音乐，而拉丁词语在阅读结束后很久仍留在脑海中。

questions.explanation: 第三段第二句说明它能在整个房间里产生迅速的音乐。

readings.title: Christmas Music and Words
readings.article:
Christmas is near, and people are actively at work in the streets. The rapid change there is easy to see. Music and light generate a good feeling, and this time can generate hope in every home.

Many Christmas music was first written in Latin, and some came from the Bible. People later put it into English for everyone. The frequency of this music is high, and each composition is easy to learn.

From another angle, we can calculate how often people use these words today. They use them at a rapid rate, but we must also keep our privacy when we talk about them.
readings.translation:
圣诞节临近，人们在街上积极地忙碌着。那里的快速变化很容易看出来。音乐和灯光产生一种美好的感觉，而这个时节能在每个家庭中产生希望。

许多圣诞音乐最初是用拉丁语写的，有些来自《圣经》。人们后来把它翻译成英语供所有人使用。这种音乐的频率很高，每首曲子都很容易学。

从另一个角度看，我们可以计算今天人们使用这些词的频率。他们以很快的速度使用它们，但当我们谈论它们时，我们也必须保护我们的隐私。

questions.evidence: we must also keep our privacy when we talk about them.

从不同角度计算这些歌的受欢迎程度，并提醒人们保护个人隐私。

readings.title: A Small Group Makes Music Together
readings.article:
When the group plays music, they watch the angle of each face and the composition of the group. A high frequency helps, and rapid practice gives sufficient time to learn each stroke of the music. They cope with small problems and keep the music clear. They also calculate the time and use a trick to remember the notes.

One member of the group had little privacy in the valley, so he used a nut and a small motor to make a trick. The trick was a good one, and it gave the whole membership new motivation to keep working together.

People can generate good ideas when they listen to each other. They must stop discrimination so that every member can join the group. With enough motivation, the group can cope with hard work and reach a good result. In this way, a small team can generate real change and do the job together.
readings.translation:
当这群人演奏音乐时，他们观察每张脸的角度和整个群体的构成。高频率有帮助，快速的练习给出足够的时间来学会音乐的每一个笔画。他们应对小问题，并保持音乐清晰。他们还计算时间，并用一个窍门来记住音符。

群体中的一名成员在山谷里几乎没有隐私，所以他用一颗坚果和一个小马达做了一个窍门。这个窍门很好，它给了全体成员新的动力，让他们继续一起努力。

人们互相倾听时能产生好主意。他们必须停止歧视，好让每个成员都能加入群体。有足够的动力，群体就能应对艰苦的工作并取得好结果。这样，一个小团队就能产生真正的改变，一起完成这项工作。

readings.title: A Family Song Before Christmas
readings.article:
Christmas was near, and the family was eager to play music together in the evening. Their music came from a Latin book in an old bible, and the composition was easy and gentle. Everyone wanted to learn it before Christmas came, so they sat in the room and listened first.

Father used a motor to calculate the frequency of each part. He showed the children the angle of the voice and said that a small voice was sufficient. They could all cope, he said, because every child would take one part. The frequency was not high, so the work was easy for them.
readings.translation:
圣诞节快到了，这家人很想在晚上一起演奏音乐。他们的音乐来自一本旧的圣经里的一本拉丁文书籍，这首曲子简单又柔和。每个人都想在圣诞节到来之前学会它，所以他们先坐在房间里听。

父亲用一个马达来计算每个声部的频率。他给孩子们看声音的角度，并说小小的声音就足够了。他说他们都能应付，因为每个孩子都会承担一个声部。频率不高，所以这项工作对他们来说很容易。

readings.title: Music in the Valley
readings.article:
One member of the group walked into a small building in the valley. He read a story from the bible and wanted to write something new. His motivation was easy to see: he hoped it would help people feel good. He used a trick to make the composition feel like home. With one stroke of his pen, he changed the ending and felt good.

Life in the valley was not always easy, and the members had to cope with many small problems each week. They kept their music to themselves, because privacy helped them feel good. A few nuts and some soup were sufficient food after a long day. They also learned to say no to discrimination, so that every person could join the group.

At Christmas, music of every frequency can generate a good feeling in a valley town. A small motor of hope keeps the members going. Their motivation is strong, and the music brings different groups together. This is the real power of music for everyone.
readings.translation:
一群成员中的一个人走进了山谷里的一栋小建筑。他读了一个《圣经》里的故事，并想写一些新东西。他的动机很容易看出来：他希望这能帮助人们感觉良好。他用了一个技巧，让这首曲子感觉像家一样。他大笔一挥，改变了结尾，感觉很好。

山谷里的生活并不总是轻松的，成员们每周都得应付许多小问题。他们把自己的音乐留给自己，因为隐私让他们感觉良好。漫长的一天过后，几颗坚果和一些汤就是足够的食物。他们还学会了对歧视说不，这样每个人都能加入这个群体。

在圣诞节，任何频率的音乐都能在山谷小镇里产生美好的感觉。一个小小的希望马达让成员们继续前进。他们的动机很强，音乐把不同的群体聚在一起。这就是音乐对每个人的真正力量。

readings.title: A Quiet Christmas
readings.article:
An actress wanted a Christmas at home with no attention, but she could not cope with the attention. She felt that the discrimination was a problem, and her privacy was gone. Her motivation was clear: she wanted a life with no attention. She decided to use numbers to cope with the problem, and she began to plan a small test.

She went into the room and put a nut and a small slice of flesh on a table. A small motor turned the table at a moderate rate. One measurement was sufficient to show the trick: the angle changed, and she could calculate the frequency in a rapid way.

She remembered her college days, when she was a quarterback on a small team in a valley. That time felt far away now. She thought about invasion, about sin, and about how people talk about a woman who wants to keep her own space. Her membership in a local group still gave her friends to talk with. One stroke of good news had changed her plan, and she felt good.

On Christmas Day, the actress showed her work to her family and friends. They gave her applause, and she felt good. She said that we can generate new ideas and still keep our privacy. The trick is to calculate with care and to tell only what we choose. Her story was a small but impressive thing that day.
readings.translation:
一位女演员想要一个无人关注的圣诞节，但她无法应对关注。她觉得歧视是个问题，她的隐私消失了。她的动机很明确：她想要一种没有关注的生活。她决定用数字来应对这个问题，她开始计划一个小测试。

她走进房间，把一颗坚果和一小片肉放在桌子上。一个小马达以适中的速度转动桌子。一次测量就足以展示这个技巧：角度改变了，她可以快速计算频率。

她回忆起大学时光，那时她是山谷里一个小球队的四分卫。那段时光现在感觉很遥远。她想到入侵，想到罪，想到人们如何谈论一个想要保留自己空间的女人。她在当地团体的会员身份仍然给了她可以交谈的朋友。一条好消息改变了她的计划，她感觉很好。

圣诞节那天，女演员向家人和朋友展示了她的作品。他们给了她掌声，她感觉很好。她说我们可以产生新想法，同时保持隐私。诀窍是用心计算，只说出我们选择说的。她的故事是那天一件小而令人印象深刻的事。

readings.title: A Christmas of Small Joys
readings.article:
The actress got up early on a morning before Christmas. She felt good because Christmas was near. Her rapid steps went down the hallway as she moved from room to room. She wanted privacy that day, so she went into a room and told no one her plan. Music played low in that room, and she did not mind it at all.

She stood in the room with moderate motivation and made a nut soup for the Christmas party. First she used a small trick to calculate the measurement of the flour, then she cut the food at a good angle. One slice was not sufficient for her brother, so she made another. She worked with care and did not lose one nut.

As she waited for the food, she thought of her school days and the Latin words she once loved. She would read the Bible in the morning and gaze at each line with care. Her friend, a quarterback, had to cope with discrimination at work. He said that no sin of the flesh should make a person feel less than others.

She drove her motor car through the valley on her way to the party. The music on the phone had a high frequency, and she liked its composition. The news told of a rapid invasion, which was not impressive. Her membership in a reading group gave her a good stroke of chance that day.

The party was a great event, and many people gave her good feedback about the food. This feedback helped her generate new motivation for the coming year. She felt that Christmas could generate good humor in small moments. For her, the true trick of the season was to spend time with people she loved.
readings.translation:
这位女演员在圣诞节前的一个早晨早早起床。她感觉很好，因为圣诞节快到了。她快速的脚步沿着走廊，从一个房间走到另一个房间。那天她想要隐私，所以她走进一个房间，没有告诉任何人她的计划。那个房间里播放着低音量的音乐，她一点也不介意。

她带着适度的动力站在房间里，为圣诞派对做了一锅坚果汤。首先她用一个小技巧来计算面粉的量，然后她以合适的角度切食物。一片对她的兄弟来说不够，所以她又做了一片。她小心翼翼地工作，没有丢失一颗坚果。

在等待食物的时候，她想起了学生时代和她曾经喜爱的拉丁语单词。她会在早晨读《圣经》，仔细凝视每一行。她的朋友，一位四分卫，在工作中不得不应对歧视。他说，任何肉体的罪都不应该让人觉得自己不如别人。

她开着汽车穿过山谷前往派对。手机上的音乐频率很高，她喜欢它的作曲。新闻讲述了一次快速的入侵，这并不令人印象深刻。那天，她在读书会的会员身份给了她一次好运。

派对很盛大，许多人对食物给了她很好的反馈。这些反馈帮助她为来年产生了新的动力。她觉得圣诞节可以在小瞬间产生好心情。对她来说，这个季节真正的诀窍是与她爱的人共度时光。

readings.title: The Joy of Singing Together
readings.article:
Christmas music spread through Latin lands many years ago, and many people learned old songs from the Bible. They tried to calculate the frequency of each note with care. Rapid changes in the music were hard to follow, but the songs were beautiful and the people loved them.

A music teacher wanted to generate new sounds for a Christmas song, so she used a nut and a small motor in her room. She turned the motor slowly, and the nut moved at a new angle. Her trick was simple: one stroke of her hand could change the sound. She smiled at the result.

In a small valley, a group of friends met each week to work on their new composition. Their membership grew slowly, but their motivation was strong. With sufficient practice, they learned to cope with the difficult parts, and their voices blended well.

Singing together brings a warm feeling that is sufficient for every member, and the group keeps its privacy while sharing songs. They say no to discrimination and are pleased to hear each new voice. Rapid growth follows when people cope with small problems and keep their motivation high.

readings.title: The Power of Music
readings.article:
Long ago, Christmas music began in the Latin church, where members used the Bible to calculate and generate simple songs for the people. Their membership grew slowly, and they sang these songs together at every winter meeting.

In a good composition, a group can change the angle of a line and the frequency of its beat. A rapid change can be a trick for the ear, and one strong stroke of the hand may be sufficient to keep the group together. They sing a short part again and again until it feels easy.

A young singer learned a good trick from her teacher. When a song felt too hard, she would picture a deep valley and a small nut in it. That picture gave her the motivation to cope, and her motor memory carried her through the difficult lines.

Music can give people privacy in a world that is never quiet, and it can also fight discrimination when a song speaks for every voice. A singer who copes with hard words can use a simple trick: sing with more power than the crowd. In this way, music is sufficient to make a valley of difference feel small and fair.

readings.title: The Christmas Song Study
readings.article:
At Christmas, a small church group met in a quiet valley to sing songs from the Latin Bible. Their membership was young, and their motivation was simple: they wanted to find the frequency of each note. Why did some notes appear so often in the old songs?

At Christmas, one member tried to calculate how often each note appeared in the Latin Bible text. He used a simple angle to cope with the long composition, and a rapid stroke of his pencil put a line under every high note. The results began to generate a clear pattern: high notes came more often than low ones.

They used a nut and a small trick to test whether people remembered high notes better. The results were clear, but the group also talked about privacy and discrimination. They agreed that one test was not sufficient, and that music works like a motor for memory.

In the end, the test showed that music can act like a motor for memory, and the group's motivation grew. Their composition taught them that working together is precious, and that being fair matters more than any trick. They left the valley with a new song and a good feeling.

readings.title: The Architect's Christmas Show
readings.article:
As Christmas came near, an architect sat in his room and worked on a special show. He used numbers and music every day. He measured each angle of the stage and wrote the composition on paper. He would calculate the frequency of each note and check it against an old Latin song in his bible. He wanted the show to be a gift for his town.

He used a continuous curve to plan the stage. He could calculate fast, and his rapid work helped the team. He did not share private data, because privacy was important to him. The design looked simple, but it was sufficient for the show. He drew each angle with care, and the stage was ready.

When he was a boy, he studied Latin in school. His teacher told the class a legend about a valley. In the legend, a gentle god lived in the valley and gave people flour and nuts. The teacher said the story was not in the Bible. He taught the boys a trick to remember the words: they said them again and again, at a rapid speed.

His membership grew quickly, and a famous actress joined the team with a young quarterback. The quarterback threw the ball to a receiver who carried boxes across the stage. A local sponsor gave them a slice of steak and enough flour, so they had sufficient food for the long evening. Everyone worked together, and no one asked for an excuse to leave early.

On Christmas night, the stage lights made an impressive invasion of the room, and the crowd began to generate warm applause. The players felt new motivation from every gentle gaze. A rapid stroke of light crossed the curve of the stage, and the whole space seemed to shine.

After the show, the architect stood in the quiet room and thought about what the night had taught him. A good plan, a gentle heart and a team that worked well together could turn a simple idea into something people would remember. He smiled, eager for next year, when they would try again with even more care.

readings.article:
The actress spent every morning before Christmas preparing food for her neighborhood. She had to calculate how many people would come, because only a sufficient number of seats would let everyone sit and enjoy the evening. Her membership list kept growing, and she began to worry that the small room could not hold everyone who wanted to join.

She called her friend, an architect named Marco, who agreed to help her plan the space. He took a measurement of the room and put each angle on a simple drawing. A gentle curve near the door, he said, would lead people in and out at a moderate speed. "This plan is sufficient for now," he told her, "but we can change it later."

The architect told her that a continuous plan would help the community cope with changes that come fast. He said the frequency of such changes was often high, and rapid decisions were necessary. "Here is a trick," he said. "Keep one helper free at all times." She wrote this down and smiled.

They sat down with an old Latin bible that her family had kept, and inside it they found a short legend about a kind man who shared food in a cold winter. The story was simple, but it helped them generate a new idea for the event. They talked about the composition of the program, and both felt that the legend gave them a gentle and sufficient plan for the night.

A former quarterback joined as a sponsor and brought flour and nuts to the room. "My motivation is simple," he said. "I was a receiver long ago, and this group helped me cope." The actress thanked him, and they carried the bags inside together before the evening began.

During the event, a guest made a remark that felt like discrimination, and the actress did not accept any excuse for it. She asked for privacy while she spoke with him in a gentle voice. "Treating people differently is a sin against the flesh and spirit," she said. Her gaze made him think, and he later apologized to the group.

The activity ended well, and everyone was pleased. They walked through the valley and the tunnel to go home. The day left an impressive memory in each mind. On the way, they talked about the next meeting and said they would come again. It was a good day.

readings.title: A Christmas of Music and Hope
readings.article:
As Christmas came near, a young actress named Maria went to church on a cold morning. She listened as a teacher spoke about the Latin words in an old Bible and about a Roman legend behind the season. The story was simple, yet it made her think about language and music, and she left with a quiet, eager feeling.

At the church she met a young architect named Anna, who often studied the building after the service. They talked about the angle of the high windows and the composition of the stone walls. Anna said the small room behind the main room was a quiet place, and she valued the privacy it gave her. The two women walked through a short tunnel under the church and agreed to meet again.

She began to study music with a gentle teacher, who taught her to calculate the frequency of each note with care. The teacher said that rapid practice, one stroke at a time, would build her skill. That simple custom gave her real motivation, and she felt her skill grow with each week.

At a small Christmas show, she met a quarterback and a receiver from the town team. They showed her a simple trick to cope with worry: go slowly and look at one gentle light. She tried it, let her gaze rest there, and her hands stopped shaking before she played. The trick was sufficient, and she felt good.

After the small show, she applied for membership in a music club, but the club told her that sufficient practice time was required. Some members said she could not cope, and she had to contend with their cold words. One man even made an excuse to keep her out, which felt like discrimination. Still, her motor would not stop, and she kept going.

After she finished the cookies, she walked into a quiet valley near her home. The river there made a gentle curve, and she stopped to gaze at it. A small gallery in the valley was sponsored by a local group, and its design was impressive. She felt a gentle invasion of peace, as if the place had a plan. The implementation of that plan seemed simple, yet it moved her.

Looking back, she saw that Christmas was not about being perfect, since no one could live without some sin; it was about sharing and never giving up. The van waiting outside would carry her home, and she felt nothing was missing in her life. Her friends had helped her generate new hope, and she thanked them with all her heart and flesh.

readings.title: The Sound of Christmas
readings.article:
An actress named Maria spent Christmas at home, listening to the radio. She heard a voice reading from the Latin Bible, and the sound was gentle and low. It seemed to generate a warm feeling in her. She did not understand the words, but the sound made her want to know more. Why did that reading feel so special? She wanted to find out.

She began to study the frequency of sounds and the angle at which they reached her ear. Each day she would calculate the differences between high sounds and low sounds, writing every measurement in a small book. She drew a gentle curve on the page to show how the sounds rose and fell, and she found the work very pleasing.

She found that rapid beats and continuous changes of sound could create an impressive feeling in her mind. To record this, she used a simple method: she wrote down each composition on a small slice of paper. In this way, she could compare one piece with another and see how the feeling grew.

She joined a music workshop on a cold morning and met an architect who spoke about the shape of sound in a room. A quarterback from a local team was there too, and he said that a good receiver must listen as much as he runs. Her membership in the group gave her a chance to share her own notes, and she left with new ideas.

At the workshop, an older teacher taught her a simple trick to protect her privacy while she practiced at home. She needed sufficient motivation, so she wrote one short stroke on paper after each daily motor exercise. Soon the small strokes helped her see how much better she was doing.

Some people laughed at her and showed discrimination, but she did not argue with them. She met their gaze with a gentle look and offered a simple excuse for her being so late with the work. "I am still learning," she said. She had to cope with their words and contend with her own fear, yet she kept her goal in mind and practiced every day.

She drove her van through a long tunnel and then down a green valley, where the road curved gently beside a creek. The festival she awaited was sponsored by a local merchant, and its booth sold cookies with a nut inside each one. She bought a slice, smiled at the seller, and felt her motivation rise again.

At the festival she told a legend about a roman leader who feared invasion and sin, saying that flesh can fail but the mind can stay strong. She spoke of the implementation of small daily steps and of what was still missing in her own practice, then ended with a moderate smile and a gentle look.

readings.title: The Christmas Song
readings.article:
The actress stood in the cold room before Christmas and looked at her list. She needed sufficient money and more membership for the community singing group, yet few people had offered help. A local shop agreed to sponsor the group, which gave her hope. She wrote a short letter to every neighbor, asking them to join and to sing with her on the last night before the special day.

One cold morning before Christmas, the actress found an old Bible in a box. The text was in Latin, and a small note said it came from Roman times. A gentle legend inside told how music could carry a message across a valley. She read the whole composition twice and felt a rapid beat in her body.

She studied the old book with care, noting every angle and frequency the writer had used. The page showed a rapid change in sound, and she tried to calculate what it meant. Each measurement seemed to follow a gentle curve, and she found this puzzle fascinating.

An architect friend came to help her measure the room, and they talked about how sound waves travel in a continuous way. The friend said a long tunnel or a wide valley can change how voices reach the ear, and a moderate space is best for a group that sings. They used a simple measurement to see how sound moves.

They used a small trick to test the sound, and the result was clear. She spoke about privacy, because some members wanted their names kept quiet. Their motivation was simple: they wanted the group to sound strong. One motor in the old piano made a soft stroke of sound, and they smiled.

A local quarterback and a wide receiver also came to help before Christmas. They carried flour, nuts and other food into the room. One man said the singing group was not for people like them, but the quarterback answered that there was no excuse for discrimination. The receiver smiled and said music is for everyone.

On Christmas Eve, the group sang in a small church, and the audience gave warm applause. Their performance was an impressive implementation of weeks of practice. An elder said the music felt like a gentle invasion of the heart. The actress watched the crowd, her gaze soft, and saw no sin in their faces. After the show, they cut the food into a slice, and the scent of warm flesh and fresh flour filled the room.

After the singing ended, she stood alone in the quiet church and thought about the whole evening. The applause had been warm, and she felt pleased with the impressive implementation of their plan. She had to contend with many small problems, but nothing important was missing now. A van would help them carry flour, nuts and other food to the next event. She hoped the success would generate new motivation for every member.

演出结束后，她反思这次经历，并计划用面包车运送物资，继续为下一次活动做准备。

readings.title: A Teacher's Lasting Lesson
readings.article:
Ms. A is an African teacher who teaches English in a united community in the south. She works hard to educate children who need help with reading and writing. Every week she holds a weekly workshop in a small room near the school. Her workshop is popular, and many children come to learn.

After school, children gather on her porch, where an old piano shines in the light. She gives each child a cookie and asks briefly about their day. It is her custom to let them choose a song, and their preference is always the same happy tune.

One morning, a serious examination in her class led to a school inquiry. A boy tried to violate the rules by using answers from a small card. The school would register the case and keep a recording of every interview. This became a controversial event in the neighborhood, and many people argued about what the right response should be.

A large proportion of the community felt worried about the examination, while others chose to shrug and overlook the problem. The odds were that most parents would call the teacher's choice acceptable, but a few still shook their heads. Some said the rule was too strict, and others said it was fair.

She did not slam the table but lightly touched it, a quiet tactic that helped her seize the moment. "I swear I will not give up on any child," she said. A hard problem is like coal, she told them, and a kind word is like a pill that slowly works inside you.

She often tells her students that Islamic customs are part of a wider culture, and that it is a grave mistake to judge them too quickly. It is evident that people who listen and absorb new ideas become brilliant listeners. To accept difference is not a bad thing; it is a strength that holds a community together.

On the last Friday of the month, a helicopter flew low over the slope behind the school, and the sun began to shine. She stood on the slope and smiled, because her wound was no longer a problem. The whole neighborhood seemed more united than before, and even the worried parents now said that her weekly workshop had helped them understand each other better.
readings.translation:
A女士是一位非洲教师，她在南方一个团结的社区里教英语。她努力教育那些在阅读和写作上需要帮助的孩子。每周她都会在学校附近的一个小房间里举办一次每周研讨会。她的研讨会很受欢迎，许多孩子都来学习。

放学后，孩子们聚集在她的门廊上，那里有一架旧钢琴在光线下闪闪发光。她给每个孩子一块饼干，并简短地询问他们的一天。她的习惯是让他们选择一首歌，而他们的偏好总是那首快乐的曲调。

一天早上，她班上的一次严肃考试引发了一场学校调查。一个男孩试图通过使用一张小卡片上的答案来违反规则。学校会登记这个案件，并保留每次面谈的录音。这在邻里间成了一个有争议的事件，许多人争论正确的回应应该是什么。

社区中很大一部分人对这次考试感到担忧，而其他人则选择耸耸肩，忽视这个问题。大多数父母可能会认为老师的选择是可以接受的，但少数人仍然摇头。有人说规则太严格，另一些人说它是公平的。

她没有拍桌子，而是轻轻地摸了摸它，这是一种帮助她抓住时机的安静策略。“我发誓我不会放弃任何一个孩子，”她说。她告诉他们，一个难题就像煤，而一句好话就像一颗在你体内慢慢起效的药丸。

她经常告诉学生，伊斯兰习俗是更广泛文化的一部分，过快评判它们是一个严重的错误。很明显，倾听和吸收新想法的人会成为出色的倾听者。接受差异不是坏事；它是一种将社区团结在一起的力量。

在这个月的最后一个星期五，一架直升机低飞过学校后面的斜坡，太阳开始照耀。她站在斜坡上微笑，因为她的伤口不再是个问题。整个街区似乎比以往更加团结，甚至那些担忧的父母现在也说，她的每周研讨会使他们更好地相互理解。

readings.title: The Teacher on the Porch
readings.article:
Ms. Boateng is an African English teacher at the United School, where she has worked for twelve years. Every morning she stands on the old porch and watches the students walk in. She likes to educate them about small daily things before class begins. Her weekly plan always starts on that porch, and the students know her voice well.

In class, she plays the piano and lets students absorb new words through songs. Her brilliant workshop turns a hard lesson into a bright game. She hides a cookie and a piece of coal under two cups, and students laugh as they guess. Even hard ideas shine when she teaches this way.

A controversial plan near the school soon worried her. Some people wanted to take down the old porch, but she believed that this would violate a local custom. The issue was grave, and she did not overlook it. She asked for an inquiry, and many neighbors supported her.

At the weekly meeting, she raised her hand to register her view on the old porch. Her preference was clear, and she briefly explained her tactic: speak in a quiet voice, listen first, and let the facts speak. It was evident that others were listening, and a few moved their heads as she sat down.

The yearly examination brought a strict inspection into her classroom, and she felt worried all week. A boy fell on the slope outside and got a small wound on his knee. She gave him a pill for the pain and told the class to stay quiet, because a worried teacher cannot help anyone.

On Friday a helicopter appeared above the school and began to shine a light on the slope behind the porch. The children ran out and tried to seize the chance to make a recording on a phone. A door began to slam in the wind, and the teacher called them back inside.

In the end, a large proportion of families said the result was acceptable, and the odds of a better plan looked good. The Islamic center in the same area also offered help. She shrugged lightly and swore to keep teaching, because every child in the united school still needed her English lessons.
readings.translation:
博阿滕女士是联合学校的一名非洲英语教师，她在那里工作了十二年。每天早晨，她站在旧门廊上看着学生们走进来。她喜欢在课前教育他们一些日常小事。她的每周计划总是从那个门廊开始，学生们都很熟悉她的声音。

在课堂上，她弹钢琴，让学生通过歌曲吸收新单词。她精彩的研讨会把艰难的课程变成明亮的游戏。她把一块饼干和一块煤藏在两个杯子下面，学生们笑着猜测。即使难懂的概念在她这样教学时也会闪耀。

学校附近一项有争议的计划很快让她担心。有些人想拆除旧门廊，但她认为这会违反当地习俗。这个问题很严重，她没有忽视它。她要求进行调查，许多邻居支持她。

在每周会议上，她举手登记她对旧门廊的看法。她的偏好很明确，她简要解释了她的策略：轻声说话，先倾听，让事实说话。很明显其他人在听，当她坐下时，几个人点了点头。

年度考试给她的教室带来了严格的检查，她整个星期都感到担心。一个男孩在外面斜坡上摔倒，膝盖上有一个小伤口。她给他一片止痛药，并告诉全班保持安静，因为一个担心的老师不能帮助任何人。

星期五，一架直升机出现在学校上空，开始照亮门廊后面的斜坡。孩子们跑出去，试图抓住机会用手机录音。一扇门在风中开始砰地关上，老师把他们叫回里面。

最后，大部分家庭说结果可以接受，更好计划的几率看起来不错。同一地区的伊斯兰中心也提供了帮助。她轻轻地耸了耸肩，发誓继续教书，因为联合学校的每个孩子仍然需要她的英语课。

readings.title: A Question About Custom
readings.article:
Kofi is an African student in a united English class. He wants to absorb every word about Islamic custom. The class is a brilliant workshop, and the teacher will educate them briefly. At first, Kofi finds one custom hard to follow, so he watches and listens.

In class, the African student asked about a controversial Islamic custom and briefly gave his preference. He did not want to violate the law, but he could not overlook the examination of his own culture. He raised his hand to register his question, then waited for the teacher to speak.

The teacher did not violate the class law, but she asked the boy to step onto the porch and sit for a minute. She explained the proportion of old customs that still matter in daily life there. A helicopter went over the school, and the boy could only shrug.

在课堂上，这位非洲学生问了一个有争议的伊斯兰习俗，并简短地给出了他的偏好。他不想违反法律，但他无法忽视对自己文化的审视。他举手登记他的问题，然后等待老师发言。

老师没有违反课堂规则，但她让男孩走到门廊上坐一分钟。她解释了那里日常生活中仍然重要的旧习俗的比例。一架直升机飞过学校，男孩只能耸耸肩。

readings.title: A New Custom in a New City
readings.article:
An African student came to a united English city last month. He wanted to absorb the local life and learn about every custom. Briefly, he walked around the streets and watched people. Some customs were new to him, and he did not understand them.

On Monday, the African student went to a workshop to take an English examination. The teacher began to educate the class about Islamic customs. She was brilliant and clear. The student raised his hand and asked a question. Then he had to register his name at the door. Outside, a helicopter went over the building.

Some people said one of the customs was controversial, but the teacher did not think it could violate anything. The African student gave a shrug. He told the class about his own preference, and he briefly explained the proportion of people with the same preference in his home city.

readings.title: The Strange Room
readings.article:
A boy woke up in an unfamiliar room in a city he did not know, and he felt terrified at once. His laptop sat on a chair, and every small thing he owned was held by a strap. He pulled the strap, and a cone fell out. Was this a coincidence, or had someone planned it?

He tried to make a classification of his things, but the plan he began to formulate was absurd: a cone beside a matrix of old keys, and a laptop under a cup. The pattern fascinated him and also made him angry, because no clear order would hold for long.

News of his strange room began to circulate among the neighbors, and their talk made his feelings rebound from hope to fear and back again. He saw his dependence on small things: a laptop as a prop, a cone on a par with a cup, and even an old story of heroin that had once terrified him. Each small dividend of rest felt precious now.

He put on his thick coat like armor and began a thorough check of every pocket and bag. The armor of a quiet mind slowly covered his fear. A thorough look at the room showed nothing more to fear, so he sat down and accepted the strange day.

一个男孩在一个陌生的房间里醒来，这个城市他并不认识，他立刻感到害怕。他的笔记本电脑放在椅子上，他拥有的每一件小东西都被一根带子绑着。他拉了一下带子，一个锥体掉了出来。这是巧合，还是有人计划好的？

他试图对自己的东西进行分类，但他开始制定的计划是荒谬的：一个锥体旁边是一堆旧钥匙的矩阵，笔记本电脑在一个杯子下面。这种模式让他着迷，也让他生气，因为没有清晰的秩序能长久维持。

关于他奇怪房间的消息开始在邻居中流传，他们的谈论让他的情绪从希望反弹到恐惧，再反弹回来。他看到了自己对小东西的依赖：笔记本电脑作为支撑物，锥体与杯子同等重要，甚至还有一个关于海洛因的旧故事，曾经让他害怕。现在每一小份休息的股息都显得珍贵。

他穿上厚外套，就像盔甲一样，开始彻底检查每一个口袋和包。平静心灵的盔甲慢慢覆盖了他的恐惧。彻底检查房间后，他发现没有什么可害怕的了，于是他坐下来，接受了这奇怪的一天。

readings.title: The Absurd Armor
readings.article:
A young man named Peter found a strange box in a dusty old room. Inside it lay unfamiliar armor that looked absurd to him. There was a heavy strap and a small cone. He put the strap around his chest and tied the armor on. The cone fit on his head, and he laughed at how silly he looked.

He tried to make a classification of the strange objects, but the matrix of shapes was too odd for any clear order. By coincidence, his friends began to circulate the news, and their dependence on his story grew. He then tried to formulate a simple rule for each piece, yet the absurd look of the armor made every rule fail.

When the news spread, the strange armor could terrify him, yet his fear did not last long. The situation began to rebound after a thorough check of every strap, and a small dividend came when a friend offered him a laptop. He put the cone on a prop and wrote the whole story down, and the odd parts were now on a par with the familiar ones.

The whole experience began to fascinate him more than he had expected, and he often said that heroin could never give anyone such a feeling. In the end, the lesson was simple: an absurd find can teach a person more than a planned lesson ever will.

readings.title: A Morning of Courage
readings.article:
Maya woke in an unfamiliar room in a city she did not know, and her laptop was gone. She tried to stabilize her breathing, but her facial expression showed fear. A Latino woman at the front desk spoke in a quiet voice, yet Maya felt far below par. She told herself to stay steady and think clearly.

At the police station, Maya gave a thorough report of her missing laptop. The officer wrote the classification of the case into a matrix on the screen and said the details would circulate through the system by the end of the day. "We are accountable for every report," he said, "and we treat each one with full legitimacy." She asked whether the information would reach every office, and he nodded. "It will circulate widely," he said, "so no one can erase it." Maya felt a little better after such a thorough answer, though she still had many questions.

Maya remembered her old job at a small clinic, where a young man had become dependent on heroin after a car accident. She had tried to formulate a plan that would prop up the clinic's budget, but the dividend was small and the cellular network in the building failed during every sweeping storm. She had wanted to help him, yet the staff could not agree on a single step.

At the clinic, Maya spoke with Leo, a colleague whose absurd jokes always made her smile. He gave her assurance that the police would help, and he affirmed that a delegation from the embassy would visit soon. "Even the Swiss team is coming," he said, "so do not be afraid and keep your hope alive."

Maya stepped onto the balcony and looked down at the street, where a row of orange cones stood beside heavy machinery that blocked the road. The sight reminded her that her coaching class was today, and that going was optional but she had promised to be there. She could almost hear Leo applaud her decision to go anyway.

Maya went back inside and made a decision: she would rebound from this morning. She strapped her bag shut, checked every detail thoroughly, and put her notes neatly into the front pocket. Her resignation to bad luck was gone. She would not live in dependence on chance anymore.

Maya walked into the crowd, and a new strength covered her like armor. The busy street did not terrify her anymore, and the noise began to fascinate her. She smiled at the coincidence of finding courage on such an unfamiliar morning, and she erased her old fear as she moved forward.

readings.title: A New City, A New Plan
readings.article:
Maya stood on a small balcony in an unfamiliar city, her old strap tight across her shoulder. She had strapped her laptop to her back neatly, as she always did, and the weight felt like a strange dividend of years spent moving from place to place. The streets below were unfamiliar, and she felt as if she were a guest in a life that was not yet hers.

Maya walked into a small classroom and sat near the back, her old strap still holding the laptop. A speaker said that the classification of heroin as a simple habit was absurd, and the words seemed to circulate through the room. The claim did not fascinate her; it made her feel uncomfortable and deeply confused about what she had just heard.

After the class, Maya met Leo, a coaching advisor she trusted, and asked him to help her formulate a simple plan for the coming weeks. He told her to stabilize her feelings first, then take a thorough look at every detail before she acted. His steady assurance made her feel less alone in the unfamiliar city.

Maya thought about dependence and what it means to be accountable for one's own choices. A delegation near the embassy raised a question of coincidence and legitimacy that no one could settle, and she wondered whether any answer would ever feel thorough enough.

Maya stood at the corner and watched the machinery of the city move without rest, its huge arms lifting and turning above the traffic. A row of orange cones marked a wide hole in the road, and she counted them twice to keep her mind steady. The crossing before her looked like a matrix of lights and lines, where every car seemed to rebound off an invisible wall and return. A sweeping wind pushed paper along the street, and she pulled her strap tighter.

She thought of armor that could protect a person from every sudden shock, yet she saw how a facial expression could break through it in a second. In the Latino community nearby, people wore Swiss watches and spoke of optional plans as if time itself were a choice. The thought terrified her and fascinated her at once, because being safe and being free seemed to pull her in opposite directions.

Maya wrote her resignation on a par with her best work, then erased the old fear from her cellular memory and chose to prop up her own voice. She began to applaud the supporters who had stood by her, and to affirm that her value and her proposal were real.

readings.article:
He woke on a bed in an unfamiliar room, and for a moment he could not say which city lay outside the window. His laptop sat on a small table, and a black strap hung from its handle. He stared at the strap and told himself that this was no coincidence, because he never left his bag open.

He sat on the bed and tried to make a classification of what he had found, but his matrix of ideas stayed empty. He wanted to formulate a plan, yet every line he wrote looked absurd. He put the laptop and the strap neatly on the desk, then read his own words again and laughed.

He thought of a time when dependence on heroin had ruled a close friend, and the memory made him stare at the wall. That drug worked at the cellular level, he had read, and no assurance could erase it quickly. He felt a wave of resignation, then told himself to be thorough and to formulate a plan before the day began.

He walked onto the balcony and looked down at the street, where orange cones stood beside heavy machinery that blocked the road. The sight terrified him, and he felt as if he needed armor against the morning. A cold wind moved across his face, and he held the strap of his bag tightly while the machines kept working below.

Back inside, his phone rang, and a man from the embassy spoke with assurance. The delegation wanted him to be thorough: he had to check how information would circulate before anyone else could act. "We will not let the story rebound against you," the man said, and the call ended before he could ask more.

He began to rebound from the shock, and he could affirm his own legitimacy before anyone else did. The plan was optional, but he chose to prop up the weak parts and stabilize the whole situation step by step. He would applaud every small gain, and he would not let fear rule him again.

He told himself he was accountable for the result, then erased the facial marks of worry with a slow hand. A sweeping quiet came over him, as if a Swiss watch and a Latino coach had taught him to accept what was only par for such a day. The dividend of that coaching was simple: he would not be fascinated by fear again.

readings.title: A New Axis
readings.article:
On her first morning in an unfamiliar city, Mia stood outside the station with a heavy bag on her shoulder. She pulled the strap tight and held her laptop against her chest, as if the machine could keep her steady. The streets were crowded and the signs were strange, and she could feel the worry on her own facial expression. She had come for a short course in financing, but now she was not sure about anything.

The girl pushed the heavy door open and stepped into a building that felt as unfamiliar as the street outside. On the wall she saw a strange classification of rooms, marked with a small cone and a matrix of lines that seemed to circulate without any clear order. "This is absurd," she said loudly, and her voice came back to her from the empty hall.

Mia met Omar, an advisor whose thorough questions made her think carefully about her goals. His coaching helped her formulate a simple plan for the week, and he would affirm each small step she took. "You need assurance that the path is possible," he said, "and I can give you that." She felt better after their talk.

He told Mia that he had worked at an embassy for several years, and that he had once joined a delegation that traveled to a distant city to discuss the legitimacy of a new rule. He said his role there had been instrumental in keeping the talks quiet and orderly. Then he smiled and said that meeting her on that very day was a pure coincidence, because he had almost stayed home.

Omar then spoke about a dangerous drug called heroin, and his voice made Mia feel terrified. He said heroin can trap a person in a deep dependence that is hard to break, and that the rebound after stopping can be even worse. His words were a serious indictment of the people who sell it, and Mia listened without a word.

The next morning, Mia joined a simulation about the textile industry, where immense machinery filled a wide hall and moved without stopping. Workers wore heavy armor to stay safe near the machines, and a coach showed how to stabilize each part before the drill began. Mia watched closely, wrote notes on her laptop, and felt the whole room shake like a living thing.

During the simulation, a heavy cone fell and hurt a worker's calf. Mia did not move away; she checked the injury and asked for calcium and a cellular phone. "Who is accountable for this?" she asked loudly. The advisor said the team would discuss the dividend later, and that a thorough review would follow, not a quick scrap of the rules. Someone joked that the worker might catch flu from the cold floor, but a nurse said he would be fine.

The whole afternoon fascinated Mia, and she began to think about her own choices and optional paths. She wanted to prop up her courage, erase her old doubts, and scrap the plan she had carried for years. The experience was a quiet turning point, and she felt that her life could finally move in a new direction.

On the balcony Mia met a Latino astronaut who spoke with quiet assurance about the axis of a turning ship and the need to keep weight evenly spread. He said that on most days he worked at par with his crew, and that no single person was above the rest. Mia listened, and the city below looked less unfamiliar.

Mia walked to the enrollment desk and said loudly that she wanted to join the training, and the staff applauded her choice. A thoughtful woman from the nursery next door brought a neatly wrapped box of spice, which seemed to divert everyone's attention for a moment. Mia signed the form without resignation, and a sweeping realization filled her: this was the first day of a new life. A Swiss advisor smiled and said the program would help her find her own axis.

readings.title: The Lost Bag and a New Direction
readings.article:
At the airport, Leo found the hall unfamiliar and the whole scene absurd, because his bag with the laptop and the strap was gone. He stood on the balcony above the hall and watched the crowd, asking himself about the legitimacy of his own claim. The strap on his wrist felt bare now, and the laptop was the only thing he truly needed.

At the airport desk, a clerk began a thorough search while I tried to formulate a clear question about my missing bag. She handed me a classification form with a matrix of boxes, then asked me to circulate the details to another office. I watched her divert three calls before she said the check was complete.

While the clerk checked the form, he thought about his old life as an astronaut, a time when his dependence on drugs was hidden from the public. He had used heroin, and the cellular damage in his calf had ended his enrollment in the space program.

At the airport, a Latino aide from a small delegation approached him and asked about his loss in a low voice. She said the embassy could offer no assurance that the bag would return, and she began to explain the financing of his insurance in plain words. He listened, though her tone felt far away from the fear that had filled him only an hour before.

Later, he found that the loss of his bag was no coincidence, and the thought terrified him. The way the empty strap lay on the floor seemed to prop up a story he could not accept, yet the mystery fascinated him. He stood there without armor, staring at the spot where his laptop had been.

The next morning, a coach offered him coaching at the airport gym, and he accepted it without much thought. The simulation on the machine felt strange but useful, and he moved his arms and legs as the coach told him to. Afterwards, he took his calcium pills and his flu medicine, because the doctor had said both were optional and could do him good. He wrote a short note to himself: take them again tomorrow.

After the coaching session, he walked to the nursery near the airport hotel, where a quiet room held the few things he still owned. He neatly placed each shirt in a box, then set the textile bags beside the wall. The old machinery in the corner made a low sound, and he put a scrap of paper under its leg so it would not shake.

That evening he stood on the balcony and found a small cone beside a metal axis near the rail. He carried both inside and set them on the table, then began to divide the dividend papers evenly among the three groups he had made. The cone rolled off the edge and hit the floor, but it did not rebound far, and he laughed at how quiet the room felt after such a morning.

At the Swiss embassy, a man with a facial scar stood near the door, and he spoke loudly to a guard who wrote his name on a list. People began to applaud when the ambassador walked in, and the sound seemed to erase the fear that had followed me all week.

Standing near the embassy door, he felt a sudden realization that he had to be accountable for his own choices, and that this was an immense turning point. The loss of his bag was an indictment of his habits, not a coincidence. A thoughtful aide was instrumental in helping him stabilize his plans, and he signed a resignation letter that would take effect at par with the coming month. He affirmed that a sweeping change was needed, added spice to his new routine, and walked out with a firm step.

readings.title: A Strange Morning in an Unfamiliar City
readings.article:
The woman woke up in an unfamiliar room in a city she did not know, and for a moment she could not remember how she had arrived there. Her laptop lay closed on a small table beside the bed, and an old bag with a broken strap hung from the back of a chair. She felt terrified and alone. Through the window she saw a balcony, and beyond it the crowded streets of a Latino neighborhood where music played and people called to one another in a language she only partly understood.

She sat on the bed and tried to make a classification of what she had: a laptop, an old bag, and a small matrix of notes on the table. She placed each item neatly in a row, but the order felt absurd to her. Then she saw a coincidence that made her stop: the numbers on the notes matched the room number. She looked at the matrix again and laughed, because the whole scene seemed absurd and yet neatly arranged, as if someone had planned it.

She recalled a medical study on dependence she had joined years before, where a doctor had tried to formulate a thorough report about heroin and its hold on the body. The talk had fascinated her then, and it still did, though it also frightened her. Dependence, the doctor said, could begin with a single choice.

Her phone rang once, and a quiet voice began to circulate a strange message about a dividend from a study she did not remember joining. The voice offered an assurance that the financing was safe and that someone else was accountable for every step. She asked who was calling, but the voice only repeated the same words and then stopped. She held the phone and felt the room grow more unfamiliar than before.

She walked onto the balcony and looked down at the street, where a bright orange cone stood beside a truck. The sight made her heart rebound with sudden fear, and she wished she had some armor to protect herself. A wooden prop held the truck's back door open, and the heavy machinery inside looked unfamiliar and absurd. She held the balcony rail tightly and told herself to breathe slowly and stay steady.

After the fear on the balcony passed, Maria decided to seek help at the embassy, so she strapped on her bag and walked quickly through the unfamiliar streets. At the gate, a guard told her that the delegation had left the city that morning. A cold realization hit her: no one was coming to help her. She felt a deep resignation, yet she refused to let this news divert her from finding another way forward.

Walking away from the embassy, Maria met Tom, an astronaut who was in the city for a short visit. He spoke with a soft voice, like a coach giving coaching to a nervous runner. He told her that calcium and cellular health matter when the flu makes the body weak, and that she should stay easy and breathe evenly. His simple words gave her a small sense of assurance.

Tom walked Maria to a small hall where a textile simulation was about to begin, and he told her that joining was optional but might help her feel useful. She sat down, and when the speaker asked for ideas about fabric and trade, she spoke loudly and clearly. A few people applauded, and one woman affirmed that Maria's point was thoughtful and worth keeping in the notes.

After the textile simulation ended, Maria knew she had to stabilize her feelings and face reality. She made a sweeping decision to scrap the old plan that had brought her here, because that plan was instrumental in creating her present trouble. The immense weight of her situation pressed on her, yet she began to formulate a simple new plan, step by step, and she felt her breathing slow evenly as she wrote each line.

She woke the next morning and made a simple decision. She would not let fear run her life anymore. Her situation was hard, but it was real, and she could face it. She looked out the window and thought about the future. A better life was possible, she told herself. She would work for it, one small step at a time, and she would not give up.

女人在一个陌生的房间里醒来，身处一座她并不了解的城市，一时想不起自己是怎么来到这里的。她的笔记本电脑合着放在床边的一张小桌子上，一把椅子的靠背上挂着一个带子坏了的旧包。她感到害怕又孤单。透过窗户，她看到一个阳台，阳台外面是一个拉丁裔社区的拥挤街道，那里音乐播放，人们用她只能部分理解的语言互相呼喊。

她坐在床上，试图对自己拥有的东西做个分类：一台笔记本电脑、一个旧包，以及桌上的一小堆笔记。她把每样东西整齐地排成一行，但这样的顺序让她觉得荒谬。然后她看到一个巧合，让她停了下来：笔记上的数字和房间号一致。她又看了看那堆笔记，笑了，因为整个场景似乎荒谬却又整齐地安排着，好像有人计划好了一样。

她回想起多年前参加的一项关于依赖的医学研究，一位医生曾试图就海洛因及其对身体的控制写一份详尽的报告。那次谈话当时让她着迷，现在依然如此，尽管它也让她害怕。医生说，依赖可能始于一个选择。

她的电话响了一声，一个平静的声音开始传播一条奇怪的信息，关于一项她不记得参加过的研究的分红。那个声音保证融资是安全的，并且有别人对每一步负责。她问是谁打来的，但那个声音只是重复同样的话，然后停止了。她拿着电话，觉得房间比之前更加陌生。

她走到阳台上，低头看街道，那里一个亮橙色的锥筒立在一辆卡车旁边。这一景象让她的心突然因恐惧而反弹，她希望自己有些盔甲来保护自己。一根木支柱撑着卡车后门，里面沉重的机械看起来陌生又荒谬。她紧紧抓住阳台栏杆，告诉自己慢慢呼吸，保持稳定。

阳台上的恐惧过去后，玛丽亚决定去大使馆寻求帮助，于是她背上包，快步穿过陌生的街道。在门口，一个警卫告诉她，代表团那天早上已经离开了这座城市。一个冰冷的领悟击中了她：没有人会来帮助她。她感到深深的无奈，但她拒绝让这个消息使她偏离寻找另一条前进的路。

离开大使馆时，玛丽亚遇到了汤姆，一位正在这座城市短暂访问的宇航员。他说话声音轻柔，像教练在给紧张的跑步者做指导。他告诉她，当流感使身体虚弱时，钙和细胞健康很重要，她应该放松，均匀呼吸。他简单的话语给了她一点安心。

汤姆陪玛丽亚走到一个小礼堂，那里即将开始一场纺织模拟活动，他告诉她参加是可选的，但可能有助于她觉得自己有用。她坐下来，当演讲者征求关于布料和贸易的想法时，她大声而清晰地发言。几个人鼓掌，一位女士肯定玛丽亚的观点很有思想，值得记在笔记里。

纺织模拟结束后，玛丽亚知道她必须稳定自己的情绪，面对现实。她做了一个彻底的决定，放弃带她来这里的旧计划，因为那个计划是造成她目前困境的原因。她处境的巨大压力压在她身上，但她开始一步一步地制定一个简单的新计划，当她写下每一行时，她感到呼吸均匀地慢了下来。

第二天早上她醒来，做了一个简单的决定。她不再让恐惧主宰她的生活。她的处境艰难，但它是真实的，她能够面对。她望向窗外，思考未来。更好的生活是可能的，她告诉自己。她会为此努力，一次一小步，她不会放弃。

readings.title: The Monk and the Changing Town
readings.article:
An old monk lives in a small town where antique houses line the streets. Each morning he takes a slow stroll before the lively market opens. Sadly, few young people stop to greet him, yet he smiles and walks on.

The monk liked to use an analogy when he talked with young people, saying that life is like a long stroll that needs both repetition and the will to revise. He told them that a curse spoken in anger is irrelevant to a quiet mind, and that repeating good acts slowly builds a strong habit.

Sadly, the town's breeding plan for the old plantation had failed, and every forecast about the bees there proved wrong. The monk saw the temptation clearly: young people wanted to breed animals quickly and forget the slow work of care. He warned them that a failed plan, repeated again and again, would only bring more harm to the land.

A governmental cleanup of the old market square became an integral part of the town's recreation plan, and the spatial design was revised so that a skate area and a skier path could share the open ground. The work was predictable in cost, yet the lively result surprised everyone, and the monk called the cleanup a useful analogy for shared effort.

At the lively recreation event, an embarrassment came when a frightened child saw a cord dangle from a tree and seemed to stab the air. People from competing groups began to summon help, yet each side spoke culturally different words, so the shared cleanup turned into a small curse of confusion.

A lifelong learner in the town tried to fulfil a promise he had made to himself, yet corrupt officials and obscure rules made his path hard. He saw that excess pride was harmful, and that predictable excuses could not hide a primitive failure. Still, he held on to excellence, revising his plan each week, and slowly the pieces began to fit.

The town has changed in ways that few could have predicted, and the old fax machine in the office now seems irrelevant to almost everyone. Sadly, some habits die slowly, but the lively market and the shared cleanup show a future that is brighter and more open than the past.

readings.title: The Quiet Joy of Fixing Old Things
readings.article:
Leo loved old things, and every Sunday he would stroll through the lively market near his home, where sellers spread antique clocks, chairs and boxes across the ground. He often stopped to touch them. "Each one carries a story," he would say, and that thought would summon memories of his own past, a past he sometimes felt was a curse rather than a gift, though he never said so aloud.

On Saturday Leo walked through the lively market, where old things lay on tables under the sun. A small antique object seemed to dangle from a hook, and its price was low. Temptation pulled at him, yet he remembered his failed attempt last year, and the embarrassment returned. He stepped back, because excess hope had once made him rush.

Leo remembered his failed attempt years ago, when he tried to fix an antique chair alone. He was frightened by every small mark, and sadly he made the same mistake through constant repetition. That embarrassment stayed with him, and he decided to revise his lifelong habit of rushing. This time he would ask for help instead of hiding his fear.

Leo went to an old man who knew antiques well and asked him how to do it right. The old man, a monk, said that fixing an old thing was like a quiet analogy: each small part was integral, and no step was irrelevant. He told Leo to look at the obscure marks and to aim for excellence, not speed. Leo listened and wrote every word down.

Leo cleared a corner of his room and thought about the spatial needs of his work, because a clean space made each task easier. He turned his work into recreation, working slowly and enjoying every small step. Sometimes he would skate in the park to rest his hands, and once he met a skier who told him to be patient. After a careful cleanup of the old wood, he felt good and ready to continue.

Weeks passed, and Leo's work slowly showed results. He could forecast how long each step would take, and his hands moved in a way that felt almost like breeding a steady mood. The old piece seemed to breed new life under his care. He thought about how people culturally pass down objects, and how even a primitive plantation tool could carry meaning. Each fix, he saw, was a small act of keeping the past alive.

When the last broken part was gone, Leo felt a quiet sense of joy that no quick purchase could ever give him. He had learned that the temptation to rush was more harmful than any broken part, and that old fears were irrelevant now. A short fax to the local governmental office asked about a small show for old objects, and he smiled at the predictable reply. Competing with nobody, he could finally fulfil his lifelong wish, and nothing could corrupt that simple joy.

readings.title: The Monk and the Antique Pot
readings.article:
The young monk lived in a quiet temple on a hill. Every morning he liked to stroll in the garden before the sun was high. He watched the bees with their busy breeding, and the lively birds that came to drink. He found these hours full of meaning and joy.

One morning Tom was walking slowly through the garden when he saw something strange near the old wall. A small antique pot was lying there, and a thin cord seemed to dangle from its neck. The pot looked primitive, with simple marks cut into its side, so Tom carried it carefully to the cleanup area. He hoped the marks might mean something, and he felt a quiet excitement as he set the pot down.

He became interested in the patterns on an antique bowl and made an analogy between them and the bees in the garden. However, the patterns were obscure, and their spatial order was hard to follow. He felt that a curse lay on the bowl, for every line seemed to hide its meaning from him.

The boy tried to revise his idea about the pattern, but each new guess felt weak and vague. He had made a forecast about what the marks meant, yet that forecast failed when he looked again. The failed attempt left him frightened and sad, and he put the old thing down.

Tom walked to the old monk and asked for help with his failed idea. The old monk looked at him and said that temptation could corrupt a young mind. He told Tom to summon his courage and to stab at every wrong thought before it grew. Tom listened quietly and felt the weight of those words.

Tom felt a deep sense of embarrassment after the old monk's warning about temptation and corrupt desires. He decided to leave the obscure object alone and focus on his daily duties instead. For recreation, he chose to skate on the frozen pond near the temple, a lively activity he had loved since childhood. A skilled skier from a nearby village showed him how to move faster, but Tom knew such competing interests were irrelevant to his true path. He returned to the garden, ready to fulfil his responsibilities with a quiet heart.

Tom saw that repetition was integral to a life he could fulfil, and he did not want excess or anything harmful. Sadly, the predictable fax from the governmental office was not relevant to his task, and competing voices could not corrupt his thinking. He thought of the plantation and the breed of bees there, and he felt that his lifelong learning, though culturally obscure, had its own quiet excellence.

年轻的僧侣住在山上一座安静的寺庙里。每天早晨，他喜欢在太阳升高之前在花园里散步。他观察蜜蜂忙碌的繁殖，以及来喝水的活泼鸟儿。他觉得这些时光充满意义和欢乐。

一天早晨，汤姆慢慢地穿过花园时，看到旧墙附近有奇怪的东西。那里躺着一个小古董罐，一条细绳似乎从它的颈部垂下来。这个罐子看起来很原始，侧面刻着简单的标记，于是汤姆小心地把它搬到清理区。他希望这些标记可能意味着什么，当他放下罐子时，他感到一种安静的兴奋。

他对一个古董碗上的图案产生了兴趣，并在它们和花园里的蜜蜂之间做了一个类比。然而，图案晦涩难懂，它们的空间顺序很难遵循。他觉得碗上有一个诅咒，因为每一行似乎都向他隐藏了它的含义。

男孩试图修改他对图案的想法，但每个新的猜测都感觉微弱而模糊。他对这些标记的含义做了一个预测，但当他再看时，那个预测失败了。失败的尝试让他感到害怕和悲伤，他放下了那个旧东西。

汤姆走到老僧侣那里，请求帮助他失败的想法。老僧侣看着他，说诱惑会腐蚀年轻的心灵。他告诉汤姆要召唤勇气，在每一个错误想法增长之前刺向它。汤姆静静地听着，感受到了那些话语的分量。

在老僧侣关于诱惑和腐败欲望的警告之后，汤姆感到深深的尴尬。他决定离开那个晦涩的物体，专注于他的日常职责。为了娱乐，他选择在寺庙附近的结冰池塘上滑冰，这是他从小就喜欢的活泼活动。一个来自附近村庄的熟练滑雪者教他如何移动得更快，但汤姆知道这种竞争性的兴趣与他的真正道路无关。他回到花园，准备以平静的心履行他的职责。

汤姆看到重复对于他能履行生活是不可或缺的，他不想要过度或任何有害的东西。可悲的是，来自政府办公室的可预测传真与他的任务无关，竞争的声音无法腐蚀他的思想。他想到了种植园和那里的蜜蜂品种，他觉得他的终身学习，虽然在文化上晦涩，但有其自身的安静卓越。

{"title":"A Christmas Conversation","article":"Christmas was near, and the town was full of light. An actress and an architect sat together in a small church. They listened as a gentle speaker read from the Bible. The reading was in Latin, and its curve of sound made the whole room quiet. The actress smiled at the architect, and both waited for the music to begin.

The group sang in Latin, and the frequency of their voices rose and fell along a gentle curve. The audience could not look away; their gaze stayed on the group. A legend led them with impressive control, and every note seemed to fill the room.

The architect was interested in the angle and composition of the sound, so he began to calculate simple measurements during the singing. He noticed a rapid change in the curve of the notes and wrote each measurement on a small card. This rapid work helped him cope with the puzzle, and he felt eager to share it.

The actress turned to him and said that privacy was the one thing she could not buy. "Being known by everybody is a continuous test," she said. "I cope with it because a small membership group protects me, and one sponsor is sufficient for my work. Without them, I could not walk down this street." He said nothing, thinking of his own quiet life.

They walked slowly along the hallway and kept talking in a gentle voice. The actress said that discrimination was still a real problem in her industry, and that she had no excuse for saying nothing about it. Her main motivation was simple: she wanted young women to cope with remarks that were not fair. The architect then told her about an impressive invasion of his office by a crowd of fans, which had been a moderate problem but also a lesson about privacy.

They walked outside into the cold air, and the valley below the church looked quiet under a gentle sky. A tunnel cut through the ground, and its dark curve seemed to lead them toward the town. In a small shop, they bought flour, a bag of nut cookies, and one slice of cookie to share. The talk was gentle now, and the simple food made the afternoon feel warm.

Christmas was near, and the continuous singing still seemed to generate heat in the cold air. The actress smiled at a small trick the group had played, and every gentle stroke of sound touched her flesh. A boy with a strong motor ran past like a quarterback, and his friend, a quick receiver, followed him. "We are not without sin," the architect said, "but tonight we are happy."","translation":"圣诞节临近，小镇灯火通明。一位女演员和一位建筑师一起坐在一座小教堂里。他们听着一位温和的演讲者朗读《圣经》。朗读用的是拉丁语，其声音的曲线让整个房间安静下来。女演员对建筑师微笑，两人都等待着音乐开始。

这群人用拉丁语唱歌，他们声音的频率沿着柔和的曲线起伏。观众无法移开视线；他们的目光停留在那群人身上。一位传奇人物以令人印象深刻的控制力引领他们，每一个音符似乎都充满了房间。

建筑师对声音的角度和构成感兴趣，所以他在唱歌时开始计算简单的测量值。他注意到音符曲线中的快速变化，并在一个小卡片上写下每个测量值。这种快速的工作帮助他应对这个谜题，他渴望分享它。

女演员转向他说，隐私是她唯一买不到的东西。“被所有人知道是一个持续的考验，”她说。“我能应对它，因为一个小型会员团体保护着我，而一个赞助商就足够支持我的工作。没有他们，我无法走在这条街上。”他什么也没说，想着自己安静的生活。

{"title":"Learning Together: A United English Class","article":"In a united english class, several african students meet each week to learn about islamic custom. The teacher, a kind woman, briefly explains why some ideas are controversial. She says that people often hold different beliefs about daily life and that open talk can help everyone understand more.

In the united english class, some african students chose to violate a class rule because of a personal preference. The teacher looked worried, though the students had a brilliant tactic: they sat on a gentle slope near the window and talked quietly. Still, the teacher said their choice was not acceptable and asked them to stop.

The teacher began to educate the class about different customs. She said a large proportion of the examination would cover these ideas, and she asked every student to register for the weekly talk. "I never swear in class," she added, "but I will not slam the door on your questions." The students listened and took notes.

After class, several African and English students sat on the porch and talked about the lesson. From there they could overlook the quiet yard below. One student shrugged when a friend asked about the grave question of being kind to others. Then a helicopter flew low above the school, and it was evident that everyone stopped talking for a moment.

The students absorbed what the teacher said and decided to hold a weekly workshop to discuss controversial ideas. The wound from their earlier argument slowly got better as they talked. They hoped the workshop would shine a light on different customs and beliefs.

At the weekly workshop, a student asked whether coal was acceptable as a gift, and another lightly played the piano while others shared a cookie. Everyone laughed, and the teacher smiled briefly. Such moments made the serious talks easier to absorb, and the group felt less worried about small mistakes.

At the end of the workshop, the students shared what their inquiry and recording had taught them. They agreed that they should seize every chance to learn, even when the odds seemed low. "Learning about others is not a bitter pill," one student said with a smile.
